h1: The 8 Best Cordless Electric Pruning Shears of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight cordless electric pruning shears, from 1.4 inch budget models to 2.2 inch units, with advice on cut size and batteries.
summary: The SEESII 1.8 inch four-mode pruner is our top pick for balancing cut size, adjustable power and price. The 2.2 inch SEESII is the one for thicker branches, and the BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX is best if you already own that battery platform. The 1.4 inch SEESII is the cheapest way to try cordless pruning.
intro: The common pruner mistake is chasing the biggest cutting diameter on the box. A shear rated for 2 inches is rarely needed in a small garden, yet it is heavier in the hand and costs more, while the shrub you actually trim is often under an inch.

We ranked eight cordless pruners using the spec sheets and what owners describe. Rated cut diameter, adjustable power modes, battery arrangement, weight and price bucket drove the order. Cut capacity is a ceiling, not a daily setting, so we favored models that match common pruning jobs.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 1.8" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: Four power modes and a useful 1.8 inch cut at a fair price.
products.description:
This cordless pruner has four modes and a 1.8 inch cutting capacity, which covers most shrubs, fruit trees and rose canes. Expect to land in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks first because adjustable modes let you match power to the branch, so thin twigs do not get the same hard bite as thick limbs. It sits above the 2.2 inch SEESII because the cut size is enough for most gardens and the price bucket is lower. The tradeoff is losing a few tenths of an inch of capacity.

Choose it if your branches vary in thickness. The caveat is that very thick limbs still need a saw or the bigger model.
products.idealFor: Gardeners trimming branches of mixed thickness.
products.skipIf: You regularly cut near 2 inches or thicker.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears 4 Modes, 2.2" Cut Electric Pruners Cordless
products.verdict: The same four modes with the most cutting capacity on the list.
products.description:
A cordless pruner with four modes and a 2.2 inch cut, the largest capacity in this ranking. Street cost falls between $100 and $200.

It ranks below the 1.8 inch version because the extra capacity costs a bucket more, and most home pruning never needs it. It ranks above the 2.1 inch brushless model since the four modes give you control over the cut that model lacks.

Buy it for orchards, overgrown hedges or thick limbs. The caveat is price and the extra bulk that comes with a larger capacity tool.
products.idealFor: Orchard owners and anyone cutting thick branches.
products.skipIf: Your pruning stays under about an inch and a half.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX* Cordless Pruner Electric Pruning Shears, 900 Cuts Per Charge, Tool Free Blade Change
products.verdict: Tool-free blade changes on a battery you may already own.
products.description:
This pruner runs on the 20V MAX battery system and lets you change the blade without tools. The listing cites 900 cuts per charge. Expect to land in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks third because the listing does not state a cutting diameter, so you cannot compare capacity with the SEESII models. What it adds is easy blade maintenance and compatibility with other 20V MAX tools, which cuts the cost if you own a battery already.

It suits owners of that platform. The caveat is that the cut capacity is not listed, so check the page before buying for thick branches.
products.idealFor: Owners of 20V MAX tools wanting easy blade care.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed large cut capacity.

products.name: Electric Pruning Shears, Upgraded 2.1" Cutting Garden Shears with LCD Display, Brushless Motor
products.verdict: A brushless motor and 2.1 inch cut without adjustable modes.
products.description:
A pruner with a 2.1 inch cutting diameter, a brushless motor and an LCD display. Expect to land in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks fourth because it offers big capacity at a mid price but no listed power modes. Compared with the 1.8 inch SEESII, you get more cutting diameter and a brushless motor, but less control over each cut.

Choose it for solid mid-tier capacity on a budget. The caveat is that the brand is generic, so confirm battery and warranty details on the listing.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting large capacity without paying for modes.
products.skipIf: You want adjustable power for small twigs.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Electric Pruner, 2 Ah Battery and Charger Included
products.verdict: A complete kit for people on the V20 battery system.
products.description:
A pruner on the V20 battery system that ships with a 2 Ah battery and charger. Street cost falls between $100 and $200.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives no cut diameter, and the bucket is higher than the 20V MAX option. The included battery and charger are the draw, since you can start without owning other V20 gear.

Buy it if you plan to build around the V20 platform. The caveat is that cut capacity is unlisted, so verify it before relying on it for thick branches.
products.idealFor: Owners building out the V20 tool system.
products.skipIf: You have no V20 gear and want the lowest cost.

products.name: Upgraded Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Diameter Cordless Power Pruner with LCD Display
products.verdict: Two batteries for long sessions at a low price.
products.description:
A 1.4 inch pruner that includes two batteries and an LCD display. Cost is in the $25 to $50 tier.

It ranks sixth because the cut diameter is modest, but it ranks above the cheapest SEESII since a second battery means you can keep working while one charges. That swap is the tradeoff over a single-battery tool.

It suits long pruning sessions in light-duty gardens. The caveat is the 1.4 inch capacity, which is not for thicker limbs.
products.idealFor: Long, light pruning sessions on a budget.
products.skipIf: You cut branches thicker than about an inch.

products.name: Kebtek Cordless Pruning Shears 25MM Electric Pruners 880G Lightweight
products.verdict: A light 880 gram pruner for people who tire quickly.
products.description:
A cordless pruner with a 25mm cut and a listed weight of 880 grams. Street cost falls between $100 and $200.

It ranks seventh because 25mm is a small capacity and the price bucket is higher than several better-equipped picks. The light weight is its argument, since holding a pruner overhead tires the arm quickly.

Choose it if hand fatigue is the main concern. The caveat is that there are no listed modes, and the cut is smaller than the 1.8 inch SEESII.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who struggle with heavy tools.
products.skipIf: You want capacity or value for the bucket.

products.name: SEESII Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Cordless Pruner for Gardening
products.verdict: The lowest-cost way to try cordless pruning.
products.description:
A 1.4 inch cordless pruner with a straightforward spec sheet. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, the lowest on this list.

It ranks last because it lacks the modes of the larger SEESII models and the second battery of the other 1.4 inch pick. What it keeps is a brand name that shows up across this ranking and the cheapest entry price.

Buy it to test whether you like electric pruning. The caveat is modest capacity and no extras.
products.skipIf: You want modes, extra batteries or large capacity.

whatMatters.detail: Cut diameter is the thickest branch the blades are rated to cut. Pushing past it strains the motor. Check the inch or millimeter figure in the title and match it to your thickest branch.
Modes let you reduce blade travel for thin twigs and open fully for thick wood. This saves battery and gives cleaner cuts. Look for a stated mode count.
A pruner may include one battery, two, or use a shared tool platform. This decides your downtime and total cost. Read the listing for batteries included.
A heavier tool tires your hand and wrist, especially overhead. A listed weight such as 880 grams helps compare. Check for a weight figure.
Dull or sticky blades give ragged cuts. Tool-free blade change makes cleaning and swapping easier. Look for that wording on the listing.

faq.q: Can electric pruners cut as thick as the rating says?
faq.a: The rating is a ceiling for clean cuts on live wood. Hard dry wood is tougher, so leave margin on thick branches.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Paying for capacity you do not use. Match cut size to your thickest regular branch instead of the largest number.

faq.q: Is a brushless motor worth it?
faq.a: It generally means less wear and quieter, more efficient operation. The 2.1 inch brushless model lists it, though other models do not.

faq.q: Do these come with a battery?
faq.a: The Dual-Battery 1.4 inch lists two batteries, and the CRAFTSMAN V20 lists a 2 Ah battery with charger. Check the listing for the others.

faq.q: How do I maintain the blades?
faq.a: Wipe off sap after use and keep them dry. The BLACK+DECKER lets you change the blade without tools.

faq.q: Can I use these on dead wood?
faq.a: Possibly, but dead wood is harder than live. Keep to smaller diameters than the rating.

finalTake: For most gardens, the SEESII 1.8 inch four-mode pruner is the best mix of capacity, control and price. The 2.2 inch model is for thick wood, and the BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX fits owners of that platform. The 1.4 inch SEESII is the cheap starter.
